recentItems.title: MINUS 51% OF RUSSIA’S OIL REFINING: Ukrainian weapons KNOCK OUT Russia’s energy sector!
recentItems.description:
Long-range operations by Ukraine’s Defense Forces have disabled over 51% of Russia’s oil refining capacity, causing a critical fuel shortage for the occupier army and Russia’s domestic market.
To offset falling revenues and keep funding the war, the Kremlin, in its draft 2027 budget, has drastically cut spending on civilian sectors — healthcare, economic support, and assistance to families with children.
At the same time, Germany, facing a direct threat to people’s lives, has moved to actively counter Russian sabotage and cyberattacks on its territory, strengthening defenses against Moscow’s hybrid terror.

recentItems.title: Everything "on plan" in Russia: Tu-95 crash, Mi-8 friendly fire & PLAGUE in Siberia
recentItems.description:
Everything is going "according to plan" in Russia: a Tu-95 strategic bomber crashes during a training flight, while an Mi-8 helicopter is reportedly shot down by friendly fire. To boost morale, 600-year-old relics of Dmitry Donskoy are sent to the front lines for "spiritual support" — only to be allegedly lost during a retreat near Lyman. Meanwhile, plague scares shake the Irkutsk region, Putin observes the military from behind protective glass, and the Russian parliament welcomes a new cast of colorful characters. And to cap off the week's "victories": the State Duma takes on a cutlet. Watch this roundup of Russian blunders, absurd decisions, and propaganda trying to spin defeats into wins.

Meanwhile, Russia attacks Kyiv, targets bridges and energy infrastructure, and threatens NATO with nuclear weapons over Kaliningrad. Russian missiles violate Moldova's airspace. recentItems.title: BREAKING THE SKY BLOCKADE! Ukrainian drones airdrop food to Oleshky and rescue animals
recentItems.description:
Russia attacks Ukrainian cities once again: wounded in Sumy, casualties in the Kharkiv region, a fire in Dnipro, and a strike on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge in Kyiv. The Armed Forces of Ukraine hit a Russian Buk air defense system, drone launch pads, and an EW (electronic warfare) station. In this episode: the frontline situation, Operation Vivaldi, and the occupiers' losses. Ukrainian troops delivered nearly four tons of humanitarian aid via drones to occupied Oleshky and rescued six animals. The EU demands humanitarian access, while Ukraine insists on the evacuation of civilians, which Russia continues to block. We also cover the elections in Latvia and Sweden’s new defense strategy. Watch the key news from Ukraine and around the world on our channel.

recentItems.title: THE ECONOMY IS CRUMBLING: 68% of Russians suddenly want the war to stop
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian drones are striking deeper than ever, and the war that Russians once watched only on TV is now shattering their everyday lives. Oil refineries, fuel depots, ports, and major logistics hubs like Wildberries and Ozon are going up in flames. Gas station queues, severe fuel shortages, and lost export revenue are mounting unbearable pressure on the Russian economy.

In this special report, "Long-Range Sanctions," we break down how strikes deep inside the Russian rear are draining the Kremlin's war chest, threatening the banking sector, and why an increasing number of Russians are demanding an end to hostilities. Can this chain reaction force Putin toward peace? Watch how Ukraine is targeting the aggressor’s key vulnerabilities and reshaping the war.

recentItems.title: Merz in Kyiv: New weapons, air defense, and support for Ukraine | LIVE
recentItems.description:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Federal Chancellor of Germany Friedrich Merz hold a joint press briefing in Kyiv.

During the meeting, the leaders discussed military and energy support for Ukraine, strengthening air defenses, joint drone production, and future Ukraine-Germany cooperation.

Germany announced a new support package for Ukraine worth over €1.3 billion. The sides also reported 15 signed agreements and documents totaling more than €8.5 billion, focusing on German defense procurement and joint security projects.

Key topics include protecting Ukrainian skies, interceptor drones, long-range weapons, energy grid resilience, and diplomatic efforts to end the war.

Watch the joint press briefing of Zelenskyy and Merz live from Kyiv.
